stem:
The diagram shows triangle $XYZ$ with $XY=10$ cm. From $Z$, Avni draws a perpendicular to the line through $XY$, meeting it at $H$, and measures $ZH=6$ cm.

Which pair correctly gives the area of $\triangle XYZ$?

options.text: Take base $XY=10$ cm and perpendicular height $ZH=6$ cm, so area $=\frac{1}{2}\times10\times6=30$ cm$^{2}$.
Report the word base as the area of $\triangle XYZ$.
Use $XY=10$ cm with a slanted side from $Z$ that is not perpendicular to the line through $XY$.
Find the perimeter of $\triangle XYZ$ from its three side lengths.

teacher.key_rationale: Area needs a base and the matching perpendicular height: $\frac12\times10\times6=30$. Naming "base" swaps the quantity. A non-perpendicular slant omits the height condition. Perimeter is outside this area hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source figure as triangle XYZ with base XY=10 cm and perpendicular ZH=6 cm.
